gazetteer_names_needed.name: Cilicia Trachea
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Rugged Cilicia, the coastal Taurus from Coracesium (Alanya, about 32.0E) to the Lamos river (about 34.2E); drawn now as a 7-point polygon (62 cells), the gazetteer's 'Cilicia' being only the plain (Adana, Mersin, Osmaniye).

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Gordyene (Corduene)
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: The Bohtan country on the left bank of the Tigris (Cizre, Sirnak, Siirt, Batman); the Cliopatria shape is used instead.

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Samsat (Samosata)
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Capital of Commagene, 37.579N 38.481E (Samsat page), now under the Ataturk reservoir; drawn as a 15 km coordinate circle because its grid cell falls in Sanliurfa, not Adiyaman.

problems: Cross-batch conflicts left for the owners (details in notes): Nisibis in 165 is lost by kingdom-of-adiabene, parthian-empire /ledger/59 and, via the Osroene shapes before the cut, was double-booked; roman-empire /ledger/107 (299 polygon) overlaps 24 of Adiabene's 98 core cells and /ledger/115 gives the 363 return to sasanian-empire while Adiabene records it as a gain from roman-empire; parthian-empire has Adiabene's Parthian vassalage from -95 (Adiabene page: -145/-141) and carves it out as a loss in -63.

Cliopatria's Commagene outline is misplaced (9 of 36 cells in Adiyaman, 12 in Elazig, 8 in Malatya, Samosata outside); kingdom-of-cappadocia (me-05) /ledger/13 gives Commagene 17 cells of its -64 shape in -63 on that basis; Cliopatria's Roman Republic -63 shape holds 24 of the 38 corrected Commagene cells (eu-03).
roman-empire keeps Commagene a client from -27 to 72 although the kingdom was a Roman province 17-38 and deposed about 40 (eu-04).

Region choices that are readings, not pages: Adiabene 299/363 as the intersection with eu-04's polygon (I preferred it to the reviewer's Nineveh-minus-Arbil form, which leaves 3 overlapping cells); Commagene's Cilicia Trachea polygon is generous (62 cells against the kingdom's 38); Osroene's Nisibis cut follows the reviewer although the Osroene page says the eastern boundary 'may have extended to Nisibis'.
The Parthian Empire page has no sentence on Mithridates II and the three kingdoms; the Mithridates II of Parthia page does (cited for -95 in the Gordyene and Osroene dossiers).
No tool failures; no pages failed to load. The mount copies were read back after writing and are unchanged by other writers.
